newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO steady to firm, India fuels support.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO steady to firm, India fuels support.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Monday were expected to be steady to firm, in line with firmer paper quotes, traders said on Monday.
Singapore September swaps were quoted firmer at $113.50/$115 per tonne against bids at around $110.50.
On the cash market, traders said cash fundamentals were healthy.
A major was heard bidding for cst 180 cargoes loading in September and October at $114-$115 per tonne.
Cst 180 fuel oil for loading in end September was assessed at $112-$114 per tonne on Friday.

They said Indian purchase of a total of 100,000 tonnes of fuel oil for delivery in September will help support the market. Traders said although more MidEast cargoes maybe heading towards the Far East in the second half of September, strong bunker demand in Fujairah may cap the supplies coming to Singapore.
India has purchased two 25,000 tonnes cargoes from a Mideast trader, FAL Energy and another two cargoes from Swiss trader, Glencore.
